title: Millenburg, Smokey Mary train, West End and courtship
summary: Getting to Millenburg and Bucktown by train, Brendan's Pavilion, and going to West End while courting her first husband.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I didn't go. My sister would go. I didn't know how they went. They went by the old train, Smokey Mary. They used to call the old train out at Millenburg. See that lighthouse at the Spanish Fort? Well, that was formerly Millenburg.
Right out there in the middle of the plate. Yeah. I know where that was.

And that was part of it. But where West End is, is where you call Bucktown. Brendan's Pavilion was in Bucktown, where the Myo Myo Club is. Where I wanted to go for my birthday and you wouldn't take me.

Well, maybe he doesn't like those drums out there. I went once and I really enjoyed it. She's been trying to get me to go out and take her out there for years. Cute. Another birthday I didn't go. Well, you'd go to Brendan's Pavilion. They had a big pavilion and they had a colored band out there. I don't know. My sister used to sneak and go. I guess she got it from my mother. My mother used to like dancing. Could you spend a weekend out there if you wanted to do? I don't know, but our fathers were too strict to let us spend a weekend.
Where would you catch a train to go out there?

You'd catch a ride up. I don't exactly know where you caught it. But I know it was—they call it the Smokey Mary because they had smoke coming out there. Because I know I've been out there already in that train. And you'd get all full of sut and all riding. It would come in the windows and all. Doesn't look like that out there in the Hallow, does it? I think West End is a beautiful place. I think it's prettier than where Spanish Ford is now. I don't know if they still have a fountain at West End. I used to go to West End to Manasseas when when I was between 19 and 20 and they used to have good music there. But they'd just put on a performance. You couldn't do any dancing then. That was when my first husband was coming to see me. But I had to be home for 10 o'clock, just when the fun would begin. I'd have to be home for nine, but those nights my father would be lenient, let me stay till 10. And the music would just be getting good at 10. And then in between the performance, I'd let you go dance. So it happened that my first husband didn't like dancing, so all I'd do was sit. So his daughter—my daughter sure didn't take after a father because he didn't care for dancing at all. Even the night I got married, he didn't dance. Yeah.
